hints: Focus on the jumps between successive values, a large jump means the next electron is much harder to remove.
Notice the 1st value is 577 but the 2nd jumps to 1980, then look again between the 3rd at 2960 and the 4th at 6190.
Remember the 4th ionisation is $\text{X}^{3+}(g) \rightarrow \text{X}^{4+}(g) + e^-$, so ask yourself which shell that electron must come from if the jump is large.
walkthrough:
**Understand what a big jump means**

Think of ionisation energy as how tightly an electron is held. A small increase means electrons come from the same shell. A large jump means you have started breaking into a filled inner shell closer to the nucleus.

Rule to look for:
$$\text{large jump in IE = change of shell}$$

**Find the jumps in the data**

Compare each value to the next one. From 1st to 2nd: 577 to 1980 is a huge jump, about 3.4 times bigger. From 2nd to 3rd: 1980 to 2960 is only a small rise. From 3rd to 4th: 2960 to 6190 is another large jump, more than double.

$$577 \rightarrow 1980 \rightarrow 2960 \rightarrow 6190$$

**Link the jumps to the ions formed**

The first large jump tells us X has 1 easily removed outer electron, then 2 more in the next shell. The second large jump for the 4th ionisation means that electron is removed from a filled inner shell.

$$\text{X}^{3+}(g) \rightarrow \text{X}^{4+}(g) + e^-$$
So the ion produced by breaking into the filled shell is $\text{X}^{4+}$.

options.A: Incorrect. X+ is made by the 1st ionisation, $\text{X} \rightarrow \text{X}^+ + e^-$, which needs only 577 kJ mol-1. This is the easiest electron to remove, so it comes from the outer shell, not a filled inner shell.
options.B: Incorrect. X2+ is made by the 2nd ionisation. Although there is a jump from 1st to 2nd, the 2nd and 3rd values (1980 and 2960) are fairly close, showing they come from the same shell. This is not breaking into a filled inner shell.
options.C: Incorrect. X3+ is made by the 3rd ionisation needing 2960 kJ mol-1. This is only a little higher than the 2nd, so it is still the same shell as the 2nd electron. Students often pick this because X is in Group 13, but the question asks for the product after breaking the filled shell.
options.D: Correct. The 4th ionisation jumps from 2960 to 6190 kJ mol-1, a very large increase. This shows the 4th electron is removed from a much more stable filled inner shell. The equation is $\text{X}^{3+} \rightarrow \text{X}^{4+} + e^-$, so the ion produced is X4+.
